recentItems.title: Young lawmakers remain the exception as an older generation dominates US Congress
recentItems.description:
Almost all US voters, whichever party they back, agree their politicians are too old.

The median age of lawmakers at the US Capitol is 64 in the Senate and 57 in the House, well above the median age of the American population, which is 39.1 according to the census.

The US Constitution sets no maximum age for serving in Congress, but it sets minimums: 30 for a senator and 25 for a representative. Democrat Maxwell Frost was elected at 25 to represent Florida’s 10th district and is now 29. He said different messengers are needed to speak to young people, and he sees more of them getting involved in politics.

But young people holding power is still the exception on Capitol Hill, where the older generation dominates.

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Zhou-Castro reports from Washington, DC.

recentItems.title: Fears of an all-out Ethiopia-Eritrea war as Tigray conflict escalates
recentItems.description:
There are fears of a return to all-out war between Ethiopia and Eritrea.

Addis Ababa accuses its neighbour of backing an opposition alliance seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government. Asmara has denied the allegations, but witnesses and monitoring groups report seeing Eritrean soldiers on the ground in the Tigray region.

In late September, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and six other rebel groups launched an offensive in Tigray, Afar and Amhara. Federal government troops and allied fighters struck back in early October, retaking Mekelle, Adigrat and Aksum. This week, the monitor ACLED reported that Eritrean soldiers withdrew across the border at Zalambessa as Ethiopian troops advanced.

The US is urging de-escalation, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling on all parties to return to the 2018 peace framework. That deal, signed in Jeddah, ended a 20-year state of war.

Al Jazeera’s Michael Appel reports.

recentItems.title: Greens for Palestine stand by Zionism motion as pressure on UK Green Party grows
recentItems.description:
The Greens for Palestine, an advocacy group within the UK’s Green Party, has stood by a motion the party passed earlier this month that designates Zionism as a form of racism. The group has denied accusations of antisemitism.

At a press conference in London, the group highlighted Palestinian voices. Lubna Speitan, a Greens for Palestine member who led efforts to pass the motion, said she has been stalked and has received death and rape threats since the vote. The motion also calls for a single state in historic Palestine.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has instructed local authorities run under Labour and Green power-sharing agreements to work only with Green councillors who denounce the motion. The party has been divided, with a few Jewish members publicly saying they no longer feel welcome.

Al Jazeera’s Camille Nedelec reports from London.

recentItems.title: Why is Congress so old? Most Americans back age and term limits
recentItems.description:
Almost all US voters, regardless of party, agree on one thing: their politicians are too old. President Donald Trump turned 80 earlier this year.

More than two dozen members of Congress are now over 80, and roughly a quarter are 70 or older. Three of the ten oldest politicians have served since 1981. The median age of an American is 39.

Voters Al Jazeera spoke to in Washington, DC, said age brings physical and mental limits, and that term limits or age limits would keep politicians motivated.

Many other developed countries have neither, yet their legislators are younger on average. The US House of Representatives averages 57.9, compared with 45.4 in Germany’s Bundestag and 49.2 in the UK’s House of Commons.

Al Jazeera’s John Holman reports from Washington, DC.
